clue.text: Commotion, having drink knocked back after drink

parts.note: a spirit; this is the second 'drink' in the clue, placed first because the other comes after it

indicators.note: a drink knocked back is downed, and 'back' tells us the second drink is read from end to start

parts.note: to sup is to drink, taken in sips

explanation.surface: A noisy scene breaks out as someone downs one drink after another.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue has two drinks; 'after' means the one named second goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: A rumpus is a noisy disturbance or uproar, a direct synonym of commotion.

clue.text: Mostly mock child showing a lack of sense

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter of the next word is dropped

parts.note: mock as an adjective means fake or imitation
a male child

explanation.surface: Someone teases a child who is behaving foolishly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mock' looks like a verb meaning tease, but it is the adjective meaning fake.
explanation.definitionFit: Unreason is the absence of rational thought, which is exactly a lack of good judgement or logic.

clue.text: Cases of aide heading for Egypt wearing shades

parts.note: PA is a personal assistant

indicators.note: something worn is surrounded by clothing, so this letter goes inside the colours word

parts.note: tints are shades of colour

indicators.note: a heading sits at the top, so only the opening letter of the country is used

parts.note: the first letter of Egypt

explanation.surface: An assistant packs bags for a trip to Egypt wearing sunglasses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cases' suggests luggage, but doctors call the people they treat cases. PA + TI(E)NTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Medical staff refer to the people under their care as cases, so cases can stand for sick people being treated.

clue.text: Knowing how one comes across dotty false pottery

indicators.note: dotty means crazy, so the letters of the next word are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
ware is pottery, as in earthenware

explanation.surface: Someone conscious of their image owns some silly fake pottery.
explanation.definitionFit: Being self-aware means having insight into your own character and the impression you make on others.

clue.text: Return of problem forces beginner to make wine

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so the word for problem is read from its end

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem
a cadet is a trainee in the armed forces

explanation.surface: A recurring problem makes a raw military recruit produce wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Muscadet is a dry white wine from the Loire valley in France, so it is an example of wine.

clue.text: Extra fat butter? It's beneath e.g. lid made fancy

indicators.note: in a down entry, being beneath means coming after the other part
made fancy means elaborately reworked, so the preceding letters are rearranged

parts.note: these letters, taken as written, are to be rearranged
butter is a spread for bread

explanation.surface: Someone asks if the butter is stored under a decorated lid, worrying about extra fat.
explanation.walkthrough: In this down clue SPREAD sits below the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Middle-age spread is the weight that tends to settle around the waist in middle years, extra fat on the body.

clue.text: Half-hearted on-screen presence back in comedy

parts.note: the pointer seen on a computer screen

indicators.note: the back of a word is its end, so only the closing letter is kept

parts.note: the last letter of comedy

explanation.surface: A comic actor gives a lacklustre performance on screen.
explanation.definitionFit: A cursory effort is hasty and superficial, done without real care or commitment.

clue.text: One's kicked lapdog for barking, but not loudly

definitions.note: read as 'one is kicked', i.e. a thing that is kicked

indicators.note: barking means mad, so the letters are thrown into disorder
but not tells us to remove the letter for the following word

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
f is forte, the musical direction to play loudly; this letter is removed

explanation.surface: A small pet dog gets kicked for yapping, though the barking is quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the F from LAPDOG FOR, then rearrange the rest. 'Barking' plays on the dog in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A drop goal in rugby is scored by dropping the ball and kicking it on the half-volley, so it is something kicked.

clue.text: Hear pop star having romantic encounters

parts.note: a judge hears or tries a case in court
Sting is the singer, formerly of the Police

explanation.surface: Gossip about a famous singer's love affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hear' invites a sound-alike, but it means to try in a legal sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A tryst is a secret lovers' meeting, so trysting is meeting a lover in secret.

clue.text: Blathered on, unnerved by pressure

parts.note: P is the symbol for pressure
rattled means shaken or unnerved

explanation.surface: Someone talked nervously and at length after being put under pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' here means next to, letting the pressure letter come first.
explanation.definitionFit: To prattle is to chatter foolishly at length, which is to blather on.

clue.text: Where order's kept, the main concern is lacking it

indicators.note: lacking something means it is missing, so those letters are taken out

parts.note: a priority is the most important matter
taken as written; these letters are removed

explanation.surface: Keeping things tidy is the top concern, but it is missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' suggests tidiness, but here it is a religious order of monks or nuns.
explanation.definitionFit: A priory is a house of monks or nuns, so it is where a religious community is housed.

clue.text: Call to engage team working in undesirable post

indicators.note: to engage is to take on or hold, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: to hail is to call out to someone

indicators.note: working suggests being worked over into a new shape, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone phones to hire staff for an unattractive job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Post' looks like a job, but it means mail.
explanation.definitionFit: Hate mail is abusive letters sent to someone, mail nobody wants to receive.

clue.text: Nothing left by husband eating a sweet

indicators.note: eating takes something inside, so this letter is swallowed by the rest
being left by someone means they have gone, so that letter departs

parts.note: nought is zero
H is the abbreviation for husband; it is removed
taken as written

explanation.surface: A wife is left with nothing after her husband walks out, so she eats a sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: Nougat is a chewy confection of sugar or honey with nuts, a kind of sweet.

clue.text: Gathering English rap covers showing culture

indicators.note: covers means wraps around, so one word goes outside the other

parts.note: a rap or tap is a light knock
E is the abbreviation for English
arty means showing an interest in the arts

explanation.surface: A social event where English rap music shows off cultural sophistication.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rap' looks like music but is a knock.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea party is a social occasion where people meet for tea, a kind of gathering.

clue.text: Means to retain worker with energy in important post

indicators.note: to retain is to hold on to, so the first word keeps the second inside it

parts.note: a tool is a means of getting something done
a temp is a temporary worker
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A firm plans how to keep an energetic employee in a senior job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Important post' sounds like a senior job; it is a carved pole of great significance.
explanation.definitionFit: A totem pole is a tall carved wooden pole of cultural and spiritual significance, so literally an important post.

clue.text: It's essential to defend soft goals

indicators.note: essential to means at the core of, so the letters lie within the next words

parts.note: found running across the two words

explanation.surface: A football coach says defending against easy goals is vital.
explanation.definitionFit: Ends means aims or purposes, as in the ends justifying the means, so they are goals.

clue.text: Keeping cold, something added to food hamper

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so the cold letter sits within the rest

parts.note: an E-number is a code for a food additive in Europe
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A picnic hamper keeps food chilled, along with some additive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hamper' looks like a picnic basket, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To encumber is to weigh down or impede, which is what hampering someone does.

clue.text: Drug that makes you go wild I tried outside upper-class clubs

indicators.note: outside means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go around the next one
wild means out of control, so the letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
U means upper-class in British usage
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

explanation.surface: Someone tried a drug in posh nightclubs and it made them wild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go' is a euphemism for urinating.
explanation.definitionFit: A diuretic increases the production of urine, so it is a medicine that sends you to the toilet.

clue.text: Without paying, get pounds in pocket

indicators.note: in places one item inside another, so the money letter goes inside the bag word

parts.note: to bag or pocket something is to take it
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Someone pockets money without paying for anything.
explanation.definitionFit: To blag is British slang for obtaining something free by persuasion or bluff, getting it for nothing.

clue.text: Smarter clothing item voguish? That is right

parts.note: a bra is an item of underwear
in means fashionable
i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Is a fashionable garment the smarter choice? That's right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smarter' looks like better dressed, but it means more intelligent.
explanation.definitionFit: Brainier means more intelligent, cleverer, which is smarter in the sense of mental ability.

clue.text: Broadcast news in America and Oz

indicators.note: in puts one item inside the following pair of letters

parts.note: A is an abbreviation for America
N, the abbreviation for new, stands for news
'n' is the informal form of and, as in rock 'n' roll
oz is the abbreviation for ounce

explanation.surface: News is broadcast across America and Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oz' looks like Australia, but it is the weight abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To announce is to make something publicly known, which is what broadcasting does.

clue.text: Person who sells record is a sorry individual

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
to enter data is to record it

explanation.surface: A record salesman is a pitiful figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sorry' looks like pitiful, but it means remorseful.
explanation.definitionFit: A repenter feels regret for wrongdoing, so is an apologetic, remorseful person.

clue.text: Soldiers welcoming European fighter's practicality

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in, so the soldiers enclose the rest

parts.note: RM is the Royal Marines
E is the abbreviation for European
Muhammad Ali the boxer, with the possessive S

explanation.surface: Troops show sense in welcoming a European boxer.
explanation.definitionFit: Realism is a pragmatic acceptance of things as they are, a down-to-earth, practical outlook.

clue.text: Row ahead — row on river

parts.note: to be up is to be ahead, as in a game
to oar is to row a boat, placed after R, the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A crew rows ahead on the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' in an across clue means after, so OAR follows R. The first 'row' rhymes with cow; the second with go.
explanation.definitionFit: An uproar is a noisy quarrel or disturbance, the sense of row meaning argument.

clue.text: Papers penned by mostly puffed up ex-president

indicators.note: something penned is shut in an enclosure, so the papers sit inside
mostly means not entirely, so the last letter is cut off

parts.note: pompous means self-important, puffed up
ID means identity papers

explanation.surface: A self-important former leader writes some papers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penned' looks like written, but it means enclosed.
explanation.definitionFit: Georges Pompidou was President of France from 1969 to 1974, a former head of state.

clue.text: Some bread sandwiches dry before I interfere

indicators.note: sandwiching puts something between two slices, so the bread wraps the rest

parts.note: a bun is a small bread roll
TT is teetotal, abstaining from alcohol
taken as written

explanation.surface: Before I can interrupt, someone makes dry sandwiches from bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sandwiches' looks like food, but it is the verb for enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: To butt in is to interrupt or meddle in something that is none of your business.

clue.text: What may be felt jacket in egregious clothing suggestion

indicators.note: clothing wraps around something, so the outer letters enclose the next word
a jacket is the outer layer, so only the outside letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of egregious
a motion is a proposal put forward

explanation.surface: A felt jacket is suggested as an outrageous fashion choice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Felt' looks like the fabric, which suits the jacket in the surface; it is the past tense of feel.
explanation.definitionFit: Emotions are feelings such as joy or anger, the things a person experiences inwardly.

clue.text: Prosperous start of week after 33% cut in capital

indicators.note: a third is cut away, so the last third of the weekday is lost

parts.note: rich means wealthy, prosperous
Monday begins the working week

explanation.surface: Wealth is trimmed by a third at the start of the week in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start of week' tempts you to take only M; it is the whole day, and two of its six letters go.
explanation.definitionFit: Richmond is the state capital of Virginia in the United States.

clue.text: Bread-maker's apprentice not opening

indicators.note: without its opening means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: an apprentice is someone learning a trade

explanation.surface: A baker's apprentice fails to open the shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bread' is slang for money, not loaves.
explanation.definitionFit: An earner brings in money, and bread is slang for money, so an earner makes dough.
